summary: Arindam Chakrabarti is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as a professor at the University of Delhi, professor and emeritus at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and chairholder at Stony Brook University.
Arindam Mondal, an Indologist, earned an M.Phil. from Jadavpur University and serves as an Assistant Professor at Shishuram Das College.
Arinde L. Jonker is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed a Research MA at Leiden University, studying under Peter C. Bisschop, Daniele Cuneo, and Jonathan A. Silk.
Arion Roşu (1924–2007) studied at the University of Bucharest and later at the University of Paris under Jean Filliozat between roughly 1965 and 1969.

Aristotle C. Dy is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned PhDs from Ateneo de Manila University and SOAS University of London (under Antonello Palumbo), later serving as an Ateneo lecturer and Xavier School president.
Aritri Dutta works in Tibetology and religious studies, pursuing an external PhD at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Henk Blezer.

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held positions at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arjuna S. R. works in computational fields, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Karnataka Samskrit University and the University of Hyderabad (PhD 2012–2017), he served as Senior Research Coordinator (2018–2019) and Assistant Registrar (2025) at Manipal Academy of Higher Education.

Arlo Griffiths, an Indologist and linguist, earned his PhD at Leiden University under Henk Bodewitz. He held teaching posts at the University of Groningen, the Kern Institute, and Leiden University, before becoming a professor at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2008.

Armand Guérinot (1872–1940) was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Lyon, having studied under Paul Regnaud and Hermann Jacobi. In 1909, he worked at the Imprimerie Nationale as an Oriental typography proofreader.

Armand Minard (1906–1998) was a French Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Paris. He was a professor at the University of Lyon, directeur d’études at the EPHE, and professor of Indian literature at the Sorbonne.

Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval (1795–1871) was a linguist who served as Professor of Vulgar Arabic at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1821–1871) and Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France (1833–1871).
Armin W. Geertz is a religious studies scholar who held posts at Aarhus University, where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2019.

Arnab Bhattacharya works in computational fields and Indology. After earning a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he held professorships at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and IIT Kanpur, and served as Centre Director at the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education.

Arnaldo Beltrami (b. 1862) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Turin. He served as a Docent of Greek at the University of Bologna and taught at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani.
Arnav Anjaria is a Tibetologist who earned an integrated MA from the University of Hyderabad (2007–2014) and served as an Assistant Professor at Amity University from 2018 to 2019.

Arnold Adriaan Bake (1899–1963) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Willem Caland. He held research positions at Leiden University and Brasenose College, later becoming a Lecturer at SOAS.
Arnold C. Taylor (1867–1955) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford and taught at Uppingham School from around 1891 to 1930.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren (1760–1842) was a historian who studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen (Ph.D. 1784). He spent his career there as Privatdocent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).
Arnold Hirzel (1861–1931) was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Strasbourg and Munich, later earning his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Ernst Windisch.
